surface_notes: Pentaspan (5-TM) glycoprotein with N-terminus extracellular, C-terminus intracellular. Two LARGE extracellular loops (~260 aa and ~290 aa) connecting TM2-TM3 and TM4-TM5 provide accessible epitopes - unlike problematic multi-pass channels. ~120 kDa heavily glycosylated (8 N-glycosylation sites). Concentrated in membrane protrusions (microvilli, cilia, filopodia). IHC reliability Enhanced. CANONICAL CSC MARKER. Sources: UniProt O43490; Human Protein Atlas ENSG00000007062; Fargeas et al., Cell Mol Biol Lett 2024
internalization_notes: ADC proof-of-concept: AC133-vcMMAF demonstrated effective internalization with lysosomal trafficking (colocalized with CD107a) and IC50 2-7 ng/ml against CD133+ Hep3B and KATO III cells. Caspase 3/7 activation confirmed. In vivo efficacy: significant tumor growth delay in Hep3B xenografts. Some cell lines show caveolae trafficking (resistance mechanism). Clathrin-mediated with recycling. Sources: Smith et al., Br J Cancer 2008 (PMID: 18542072); Nature Sci Rep 2019
therapeutic_window_notes: CSC marker in GBM, colorectal, HCC, pancreatic (>=50%), gastric, cholangiocarcinoma (>=50% - best indication), lung, TNBC, ovarian, melanoma. CRITICAL: marker for NORMAL stem cells - HSCs, endothelial progenitors, neural stem cells, intestinal stem cells, renal progenitors. High retinal (cone photoreceptors ~1157 nCPM). HETEROGENEOUS tumor expression - only CSC subpopulation (1-5%) positive. Sources: Human Protein Atlas; Smith et al. 2008; CSC literature
pk_notes: CD133 actively released in membrane particles (prominosomes): microvesicles (50-600nm) from microvilli/cilia, exosomes, midbody vesicles. CD133+ particles in CSF, urine, saliva, seminal fluid. Elevated in GBM patient CSF. Creates potential decoy. Expression on circulating HSPCs (rare ~0.07% PBMCs) but NOT on mature RBCs or platelets. LOW COPY NUMBER (~10^3 vs HER2 ~10^6) is major limitation. Sources: J Nanobiotechnology 2025; Marzesco et al., J Cell Sci 2005; Bauer et al., EMBO Mol Med 2011
safety_notes: NOT pan-essential in DepMap. Prom1-/- mice viable and fertile with only retinal phenotype. CRITICAL: PROM1 mutations cause inherited RETINAL DYSTROPHIES including Retinitis Pigmentosa 41 (blindness by 3rd decade), Macular Dystrophy Retinal 2, Stargardt Disease 4, Cone-Rod Dystrophy 12 - HIGH RISK of ocular toxicity. HSC expression creates bone marrow toxicity risk. NOT tumor suppressor - promotes CSC maintenance. Sources: OMIM #604365, #612095, #608051; Zacchigna et al., J Neurosci 2009
competition_notes: No active CD133 ADC clinical trials. Seattle Genetics AC133-vcMMAF published 2008 but NOT advanced clinically - therapeutic window concerns from normal stem cell expression. CAR-T approaches in early clinical development. ICT-121 dendritic cell vaccine in GBM trials. 293C3-SDIE Fc-enhanced mAb preclinical. Absence of advanced ADC programs reflects therapeutic window challenges. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; Smith et al. 2008; pipeline databases
bispecific_rationale: Normal HSC and retinal expression requires AND-gate with tumor-selective antigen (EGFR, EpCAM). EGFR provides bulk tumor binding; CD133 arm directs payload to resistant CSC niche. Similar to MCLA-158 approach for LGR5.
key_concerns: Normal HSC expression - BM toxicity; High retinal expression with genetic disease support (blindness); Prominosome shedding - drug sink; Heterogeneous expression; Low copy number requiring PBD payloads
recommendation: Strong CSC rationale with ADC PoC. Cholangiocarcinoma best indication (>50% CD133+). AND-gate bispecific with EGFR/EpCAM essential. Ultra-potent payload (PBD) needed for low copy number. Ocular/hematologic monitoring required.

surface_notes: Unique dual-anchor topology: N-terminal cytoplasmic tail, TM domain, ~100 aa extracellular coiled-coil domain, C-terminal GPI anchor. Crystal structure PDB 3NWH shows parallel dimeric coiled coil. Lipid raft-associated on apical plasma membrane. Large accessible ECD. Sources: UniProt; Kupzig et al., J Biol Chem 2003; Schubert et al., PNAS 2010; PDB 3NWH
internalization_notes: Excellent via clathrin-mediated endocytosis from lipid rafts. Dual YxY motif in cytoplasmic domain mediates direct AP2 (alpha-adaptin) interaction. Rapid ~15 min constitutive cycling. Lysosomal trafficking confirmed via ESCRT pathway. Chugai anti-HM1.24 demonstrated rapid antigen-dependent internalization. Short plasma half-life (7.5-28.6h cynomolgus). Sources: Masuyama et al., J Biol Chem 2009; Iwabu et al., J Biol Chem 2009
therapeutic_window_notes: Overexpressed in myeloma, breast (metastasis, 70%), lung, RCC, endometrial, GI, GBM, HNSCC, bladder. HPV+ CERVICAL: massive IFN-induced upregulation creates pseudo-virus-specific tumor antigen. However ubiquitous (Tau 0.33): hepatocytes, pneumocytes, endothelium, immune cells. IFN-inducible creates variability. Sources: Human Protein Atlas; Erikson et al., PNAS 2011; Ozaki et al., Blood 1997/1999
pk_notes: Favorable: No significant shedding due to dual TM/GPI anchors. No soluble HM1.24 in serum. However expressed on immune cells: pDCs (BST2 is PDCA-1 marker), monocytes, granulocytes, B cells, NK cells. Rapid target-mediated clearance (nonlinear PK). Sources: OMIM; Ozaki et al. 1999; Chugai PK studies
safety_notes: NOT essential. BST2 KO mice viable with slightly elevated viral loads, reduced IFN-I production by pDCs, no major abnormalities. No Mendelian diseases. NOT tumor suppressor. Hepatocyte expression creates liver toxicity concern. Antiviral tetherin function (restricts HIV budding) is theoretical concern. Sources: OMIM #600534; DepMap; mouse KO studies
competition_notes: Chugai/Roche HM1.24 had extensive preclinical development and Phase I for myeloma (1990s-2000s). Program discontinued ~2018 as BCMA ADCs (belantamab mafodotin) overtook HM1.24. HM1.24-ETA immunotoxin tested preclinically. No current active Phase II/III. Solid tumor opportunity underexplored. Sources: Ozaki et al., Blood 1997/1999; Fierce Biotech; Ishiguro et al., Cancer Sci 2010
bispecific_rationale: Ubiquitous expression requires AND-gate. For HPV+ cervical: pair with Tissue Factor - tumor expresses both; platelets express TF but lack high BST2 levels. Reduces TF-related bleeding risk while maintaining efficacy.
key_concerns: Ubiquitous expression - low tumor selectivity; Hepatocyte expression - liver toxicity risk; Immune cell expression - PK impact and immunosuppression; Historical Phase I discontinued
recommendation: Excellent ADC biology (internalization, lysosomal delivery, no shedding) but narrow therapeutic window. HPV+ cervical cancer is best opportunity due to virus-induced massive upregulation. Bispecific with TF recommended.

surface_notes: Type I single-pass TM. In NORMAL cells: >98% intracellular on lysosomal membrane (only 1-2% at plasma membrane). Sub-nM cytotoxicity achieved in preclinical. Sources: Creative Biolabs; Wiley Traffic (Cook 2004)
therapeutic_window_notes: Ubiquitous INTRACELLULAR expression but COMPARTMENTAL SELECTIVITY (surface vs lysosomal) provides targeting rationale. LAMP1 among top 5 ADC targets by RNA expression in breast cancer metastases. The "reverse topology" (intracellular in normal, surface in cancer) is unique advantage. Sources: Human Protein Atlas; Nature Communications 2025

bispecific_rationale: Prior monospecific FAILED. LAMP1 serves best as secondary "lysosomal anchor" in bispecific format. Strategy: Bind surface marker first; upon internalization, LAMP1 arm binds LAMP1 in late endosome/lysosome ensuring complex is RETAINED and degraded rather than recycled back to surface (as happens with HER2, TfR). AND-gate required to overcome SAR428926 limitations.
key_concerns: Prior Phase I/II program discontinued; immune cell expression (platelets, lymphocytes); ubiquitous intracellular expression
recommendation: CONDITIONAL - Tier 2 "Lysosomal Anchor". Excellent trafficking biology but monospecific approach FAILED (SAR428926). Bispecific AND-gate with tumor-restricted antigen could overcome limitations. Use as secondary arm for lysosomal retention.

protein_name: Cadherin EGF LAG Seven-Pass G-type Receptor 1 (Adhesion GPCR)
surface_notes: 7-TM Adhesion GPCR with MASSIVE extracellular region (9 cadherin repeats, 7 EGF-like repeats, 2 laminin G domains). Strictly localizes to cell-cell junctions (adherens junctions) in polarized epithelia—sterically hindered from antibody binding. Upregulated in ovarian cancer. Sources: Human Protein Atlas; OMIM 604523; PubMed 38070011
internalization_notes: CRITICAL BOTTLENECK. As junctional adhesion protein, designed for STABILITY not cycling. Internalization is cell-cycle dependent: PLK1 phosphorylation triggers internalization only during MITOSIS (M-phase specific uptake). Interphase cells = static receptor. Limits efficacy to actively dividing cells only. Sources: PMC7808676; PNAS
therapeutic_window_notes: Upregulated in ovarian cancer (Priority 2) with poor prognosis. BUT: essential for polarity of hair follicles and skin, neural tube development. High expression in normal skin and nervous system. Sources: PMC9878842; OMIM
pk_notes: Adhesion GPCRs contain GAIN domain undergoing autoproteolysis. Massive ectodomain (~2500 aa) can be shed = large decoy. Expression enriched on B-cells = potential sink. Sources: PMC papers
safety_notes: Essential developmental gene. Loss-of-function mutations cause NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS (spina bifida, craniorachischisis) and lymphatic malformation-9 (OMIM 619319). Risk of cutaneous toxicity (alopecia, rash), potential neurotoxicity. Sources: OMIM 604523; PMC9878842
competition_notes: No ADC programs. Research focused on developmental biology and Wnt/PCP signaling. Sources: Literature
bispecific_rationale: Claude excludes due to 7TM topology and internalization issues. Gemini suggests AND-gate (CELSR1 x MUC16/FOLR1) for ovarian. Given multiple red flags, NOT recommended.
key_concerns: DISPUTED: 7-TM topology limits epitope access; junctional localization sterically hinders antibody; M-phase only internalization; neural tube defect genetic disease; skin/nerve normal expression
recommendation: EXCLUDED - 7-TM adhesion GPCR topology with junctional localization severely limits ADC feasibility. M-phase restricted internalization. Essential developmental gene with neural tube defect risk.

pk_notes: No known shedding. Expression on activated macrophages (lower than tumor). Astrocyte expression in brain. Sources: Cell Signaling Technology; PubMed

surface_notes: Type I TM with Ig-like ECD and lysosomal targeting signals. In normal epithelium (liver, intestine), LSR is strictly localized to tricellular tight junctions, sequestered from circulating antibodies. In tumors (ovarian, breast, mesothelioma), loss of polarity exposes LSR across entire cell surface—"topological switch" creates intrinsic therapeutic window. Strong IHC membrane localization in OVCAR3, NOVC-7C. Sources: UniProt Q86X29; Kanda et al. Neoplasia 2023; Frontiers Oncology 2025
internalization_notes: Excellent ADC validation. Anti-LSR mAb (#16-6) and LSR-ADC rapidly internalize with co-localization with LAMP1/CD107a in OVCAR3 cells. Dileucine lysosomal targeting signal in cytoplasmic domain supports efficient delivery. LSR-ADC (MMAE) showed potent in vitro and in vivo efficacy with tumor regression. Sources: Kanda et al. Neoplasia 2023 (PMID: 36413881); Hiramatsu Cancer Res 2018
therapeutic_window_notes: Strong tumor overexpression: ovarian (60-73%), gastric (73%), endometrial (67%), colon, bladder. Liver expression concern in hepatocytes (original identification as lipoprotein receptor), but junctional sequestration means accessible protein pool in healthy liver is LOW. High-dose preclinical (24 mg/kg) showed no hepatotoxicity. Sources: Human Protein Atlas; Sugase Oncotarget 2018; Patent US10174111B2
pk_notes: No evidence of shedding. Stable membrane localization (C. difficile toxin CDT receptor). Not on circulating blood cells. Preclinical studies showed no adverse effects on normal organs or lipid metabolism. Sources: OMIM; Cancer Res 2018
safety_notes: LSR-null is embryonic lethal in mice; heterozygous mice show hyperlipidemia. LSR mutations associated with cholestasis. NOT a tumor suppressor—high expression correlates with poor prognosis. Not pan-essential in DepMap. Sources: OMIM 616582
competition_notes: Academic preclinical program (Osaka University) with anti-LSR mAb and LSR-ADC (MMAE). Patent issued US10174111B2. Anti-LSR-DM1 construct described. No clinical trials registered. First-in-class opportunity. Sources: Neoplasia 2023; ClinicalTrials.gov; Frontiers Oncology 2025
bispecific_rationale: AND-gating with tumor-selective marker could reduce liver uptake. Proposed pairings: LSR x FZD6 (Wnt-active stems in mesothelioma/HNSCC), LSR x EMP2 ("Stealth ADC" for mesothelioma/ovarian cross-linking distinct membrane domains).
key_concerns: Liver expression in hepatocytes; embryonic lethality in knockout mice; academic-stage only
recommendation: RECOMMENDED - Strong Tier 1 candidate. Topological switch (junctional sequestration in normal vs exposed in tumor) provides intrinsic therapeutic window. Validated ADC PoC with lysosomal trafficking. Priority for ovarian, mesothelioma, gastric.

surface_notes: Type I TM with large ECD (6 cadherin repeats, ~900 aa). IHC confirms membrane localization in brain endothelial cells, glioma, neurons. Favorable topology for antibody binding. Sources: UniProt Q9UN70; Dilling et al., J Cereb Blood Flow Metab 2017
internalization_notes: No published antibody-mediated internalization data. Protocadherins form stable homophilic trans-interactions. Cadherin family generally slow-internalizing. P-Cadherin ADC PCA062 discontinued for insufficient efficacy. Sources: ADC landscape review 2023
therapeutic_window_notes: TUMOR SUPPRESSOR: silenced by methylation in 60.7% CRC, downregulated in ccRCC, pheochromocytoma. In gliomas, overexpressed but high expression = better prognosis. High normal expression in all brain regions. Not expressed in priority indications (cervical, CCA, HNSCC, mesothelioma). Sources: PMC9330298; Biorxiv 2024.08.26.609687
pk_notes: ECD cleaved by ADAM10/gamma-secretase creating potential soluble decoy. Brain endothelial expression represents significant antigen sink. No blood cell expression. Sources: PMC5624389
safety_notes: Pcdhg C-type isoforms required for postnatal survival in mice. Regulates cortical interneuron programmed cell death. KO in BMECs increases paracellular permeability and reduces BBB barrier function. Associated neurodevelopmental disorders (OMIM 603627). Sources: eLife 2020; PMC9241426
competition_notes: No ADC programs. P-Cadherin ADC PCA062 (cadherin family precedent) discontinued. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: Calcium-dependent cell adhesion. Uniquely inhibits canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling among gamma-Pcdh isoforms via Axin1 binding. Also inhibits mTOR signaling. Critical for cortical interneuron survival and BBB integrity. Sources: Mah et al., Sci Rep 2016; eLife 2020
oncogenic_notes: DEFINITIVE TUMOR SUPPRESSOR. Silenced by methylation in CRC, acts as metastasis suppressor in ccRCC (via mTOR/HIF2alpha). Expression loss characterizes malignant progression. Sources: Dallosso et al., 2012; Mah et al., 2016; Biorxiv 2024.08.26.609687
isoforms_notes: One of 22 genes in Pcdhg cluster. Each variable exon encodes unique ECD and TM domain; all share constant region intracellular exons. No soluble or tumor-specific isoforms. Sources: NCBI Gene 5098; Ensembl ENSG00000240184
toolbox_notes: Antibodies: Sigma clone 1C4; Boster Bio (WB/FACS/IHC). Cell lines: U343, 786-O, RCC4, U87. Pcdhg conditional KO mice exist. No ADC benchmarks. Sources: Sigma SAB1404174; PMC9330298
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- target absent from tumors due to epigenetic silencing.
key_concerns: Tumor suppressor silenced in target cancers; high brain/BBB expression; required for neuronal survival; no internalization data; P-Cadherin ADC failed clinically
recommendation: Fundamentally incompatible with ADC targeting. Tumor suppressor biology means absent in tumors and present in critical normal tissues.

surface_notes: Multi-pass with 11 TM helices (cryo-EM confirmed: PDB 8EHX, 8XW4). Minimal extracellular surface-accessible area. Short loops connecting TM helices. Multi-pass topology with tiny ECLs is absolute disqualifier. Sources: PDB 8EHX; Nature Struct Mol Biol 2024; HPA
internalization_notes: No antibody-mediated internalization data. No anti-ECD antibodies exist to test. Naturally localizes to lysosomes but no accessible epitope for antibody binding. Sources: Nature Struct Mol Biol 2024
therapeutic_window_notes: Ubiquitous expression; no tumor selectivity. Expressed in brain, lung, kidney, intestine. HPA: low tissue specificity. No evidence of overexpression in any priority cancer type. Sources: HPA ENSG00000137216; Neuron 2025
pk_notes: Not expected to be shed (tightly membrane-integrated). HPA reports immune cell expression -- potential sink. Multi-pass topology provides no targetable epitope. Sources: HPA; GeneCards
safety_notes: Severe LOF phenotypes: DEE118 (drug-resistant epilepsy, developmental delay, spastic quadriparesis). Mouse KO: progressive hearing loss, thirst/water homeostasis deficits, respiratory failure, impaired intestinal function. Essential for osmoregulation, hearing, respiration. Sources: AJHG 2023 (DEE118); Neuron 2025; JCI 2024
competition_notes: No ADC programs. Complete absence reflects unsuitable multi-pass topology. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: Mechanosensitive calcium-permeable cation channel. Functions: hyperosmolar sensor for thirst (subfornical organ), lipid scramblase, lung surfactant secretion mediator, intestinal motility regulator. Sources: Nature Struct Mol Biol 2024; Neuron 2025; JCI 2024
oncogenic_notes: No clear oncogenic role. Overexpression in HEK293T enhanced cell migration. One publication describes as 'frequently overexpressed in cancer' without systematic analysis. No driver role in priority indications. Sources: Biochemistry 2019; Nat Commun 2023
isoforms_notes: RNA editing affects splicing patterns. Multiple transcript variants, all predicted multi-pass TM. No soluble or tumor-specific isoforms. Sources: J Biol Chem 2020; AJHG 2023
toolbox_notes: Research antibodies exist but target intracellular epitopes. No validated anti-ECD antibodies. Tmem63b KO mice available. Cryo-EM structures available. No tumor cell lines with validated surface expression. No ADC benchmarks. Sources: Santa Cruz; PDB
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- no extracellular epitope accessible for antibody binding.
key_concerns: 11-TM multi-pass topology; no validated anti-ECD antibodies; ubiquitous expression; severe LOF phenotypes (epilepsy, hearing loss, respiratory failure); no oncogenic role
recommendation: Absolute exclusion. 11-TM topology eliminates antibody-based targeting; ubiquitous expression and severe LOF phenotypes compound this.

protein_name: Transmembrane Protein 30A (CDC50A, P4-ATPase Flippase Complex Beta Subunit)
surface_notes: Type III membrane protein (2 TM domains, single ~200 aa ECL). Favorable ECD size. However, significant fraction resides intracellularly (ER, endosomes), chaperoning P4-ATPases. Accessible surface density lower than total expression suggests. Sources: OMIM 611028; Segawa et al., J Biol Chem 2018
internalization_notes: No antibody-mediated internalization data. TMEM30A cycles between PM and endosomes during normal function. Deficiency impairs EGF and transferrin endocytosis. No ADC PoC. Sources: GeneCards; PMC10464243
therapeutic_window_notes: UBIQUITOUS in all normal tissues. RT-PCR in all mouse tissues. HPA: granular cytoplasmic expression in most tissues. TMEM30A loss, not overexpression, is the cancer pattern (DLBCL). No tumor-selective overexpression. Sources: HPA ENSG00000112697; Zhang et al., 2017
pk_notes: Not expected to be shed. Expressed on hematopoietic cells -- KO causes PS exposure and macrophage engulfment. Blood cell expression = significant antigen sink. Sources: Li et al., Am J Pathol 2018; PNAS 2024
safety_notes: Global KO embryonic lethal. Panneuronal KO also embryonic lethal. Retinal KO: complete retinal degeneration. Hepatic KO: intrahepatic cholestasis. Essential for 10+ P4-ATPases. Sources: OMIM 611028; Nature Med 2020; Liu et al., Am J Pathol 2017
competition_notes: No ADC programs. Absence reflects unfavorable biology. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: Obligate beta-subunit of P4-ATPase flippase complexes catalyzing phosphatidylserine/PE translocation. Maintains fundamental membrane phospholipid asymmetry in all eukaryotic cells. Partners with 10+ P4-ATPase alpha subunits. Loss exposes PS (eat-me signal). Sources: GeneCards; OMIM; UniProt Q9NV96
oncogenic_notes: CONFIRMED TUMOR SUPPRESSOR in DLBCL (Nature Med 2020). Biallelic LOF mutations in 11% DLBCL. GISTIC identifies TMEM30A locus as significantly deleted. TMEM30A loss increases BCR signaling and enables immune evasion via PS-mediated TIM-3 inhibition. No oncogenic role in solid tumors. Sources: Nature Med 2020; PNAS 2024
isoforms_notes: Three isoforms by alternative splicing (canonical 361 aa). Paralog TMEM30B exists. No soluble or tumor-specific isoforms. All share ECL domain. Sources: UniProt Q9NV96
toolbox_notes: Polyclonal anti-ECD antibodies available (Creative Diagnostics). Nature Med 2020 noted absence of reliable TMEM30A antibody for KO verification. Cell lines: DOHH-2, Karpas422 (hematological). CRISPR KO vectors and conditional KO mice available. No ADC benchmarks. Sources: Nature Med 2020; Creative Diagnostics
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- ubiquitous expression; tumor suppressor biology.
key_concerns: Tumor suppressor in DLBCL; ubiquitous expression; embryonic lethal KO; essential for membrane biology; hematopoietic sink; no reliable antibodies
recommendation: Fails on multiple absolute criteria: tumor suppressor, ubiquitously expressed, essential for membrane biology in every cell type.

surface_notes: Multi-pass (14 TM domains). Small ECLs. Third ECL (TM5-TM6) is largest, serves as murine leukemia virus receptor confirming extracellular positioning. N-glycosylation confirmed in this loop. Anti-CAT1 mAbs (CA1-CA5) validate surface binding by flow cytometry. Sources: Closs et al., 2006; PMC7894011
internalization_notes: Anti-CAT1 mAbs (CA1-CA5, PMC7894011) demonstrate rapid internalization upon binding. Transporter constitutive cycling facilitates endocytosis. Related SLC3A2/CD98 has successful ADC PoC. No lysosomal trafficking data specific to SLC7A1. Sources: PMC7894011; PMC11088350
therapeutic_window_notes: Ubiquitous in non-hepatic tissues. Overexpressed in ovarian cancer (IHC confirmed), CRC (>70% samples), breast cancer, meningioma, cervical cancer. Ovarian cancer data strongest for priority indications. Ubiquitous baseline narrows window. Sources: PMC9484923; Cancer Med 2024; HPA
pk_notes: Not expected to be shed (14-TM, intracellular termini). SLC7A1 is primary arginine transporter in T cells -- T cell expression creates significant antigen sink. Small ECLs mean per-cell antibody-accessible epitope density is low. Sources: Werner et al., 2016; GeneCards
safety_notes: Slc7a1 KO mice die at postnatal day 1 (severe anemia, defective erythropoiesis). Essential gene. Knockdown impairs T cell proliferation (immunosuppression risk). Critical for arginine transport feeding NO synthesis, polyamine biosynthesis, mTORC1 signaling. Sources: MGI:88117; Nature Cell Death Discovery 2025
competition_notes: No existing ADC programs. Related: anti-SLC3A2/CD98 ADC has preclinical efficacy in HNSCC. Anti-CAT1 mAbs (CA2) show unconjugated antitumor activity in CRC xenografts. Sources: PMC7894011; PMC11088350
physiology_notes: Primary high-affinity transporter for cationic amino acids (arginine, lysine, ornithine). Sodium-independent facilitated diffuser (system y+). KM=0.11 mM for arginine. Feeds arginine into NO synthesis, polyamine biosynthesis, mTORC1 signaling. Sources: UniProt P30825; Nature Commun 2018
oncogenic_notes: Oncogene-like profile. Overexpressed in ovarian cancer (promotes proliferation, invasion, cisplatin resistance via MAPK/ERK and EMT). Anti-SLC7A1 mAb showed antitumor activity in CRC. Supports tumor metabolic reprogramming. NOT a tumor suppressor -- tumors are addicted to its expression. Sources: PMC9484923; Cancer Med 2024
isoforms_notes: 11 Ensembl transcripts. Canonical 629 aa. Functions as monomer (unlike LAT family). No known soluble isoforms or tumor-specific variants. Sources: GeneCards
toolbox_notes: Anti-CAT1 mAbs (CA1-CA5, rat, research-grade) validated for flow cytometry, internalization, in vivo antitumor. Proteintech 14195-1-AP (WB/IHC). Cell lines: SKOV3, OVCAR3, MCF-7, FADU, SCC15. Slc7a1 KO mice die at birth (conditional KO needed). No ADC benchmarks. Sources: PMC7894011; Proteintech
bispecific_rationale: SLC7A1 as internalizing Driver arm in AND-gate format. Tumor metabolic addiction prevents target downregulation. Pair with tumor-restricted Anchor. Alternative: SLC3A2/CD98 (same biological axis, Type I TM, existing ADC PoC).
key_concerns: 14-TM multi-pass topology (mitigated by CA1-CA5 mAb data); neonatal lethal KO; T cell expression (sink + immunosuppression); ubiquitous baseline; research-grade mAbs only
recommendation: Conditional: only oncogenic gene in E1 batch with validated antibody accessibility. Anti-CAT1 mAbs overcome topology barrier. Safety/PK profile needs experimental validation. Consider SLC3A2/CD98 as alternative in same biological axis.

surface_notes: Primarily intracellular actin-crosslinking protein. No annotated TM domain, no signal peptide (UniProt P21333). Single study (Bachmann 2006) reported surface FLNA on neuroblastoma cells -- not independently validated. Contradicts established cytoskeletal function. Sources: UniProt P21333; Bachmann et al., Cancer Sci 2006
internalization_notes: No data. Without validated transmembrane topology, ADC delivery is fundamentally questionable. Sources: Bachmann et al., Cancer Sci 2006
therapeutic_window_notes: Ubiquitous. High in cardiovascular system, smooth muscle, brain, platelets, immune cells. HPA: low tissue specificity. Cancer overexpression is intracellular, not surface. No surface-level therapeutic window. Sources: HPA ENSG00000196924; OMIM 300017
pk_notes: FLNA cleaved by calpain (190+90 kDa fragments) released extracellularly. Soluble FLNA in plasma from breast/astrocytoma patients = circulating decoy. Platelet and immune cell expression = massive sink. Sources: Bu et al., 2012; PMC3386001
safety_notes: Essential gene. Hemizygous LOF: embryonic lethal. Heterozygous females: periventricular nodular heterotopia. Complete KO: embryonic lethal with cardiac malformations. Critical for cardiovascular development, neuronal migration, platelet function. Dual oncogene/TSG role. Sources: OMIM 300017; Hart et al. 2006
competition_notes: No ADC programs. Only historical use of natural IgM anti-NB-p260 in small Phase I/II neuroblastoma trial (Schmitt et al. 1999). Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: 280 kDa actin-crosslinking protein forming orthogonal actin networks in cortical cytoplasm. Most ubiquitous filamin isoform (X-linked). Anchors >90 transmembrane proteins to actin cytoskeleton. Critical for cell shape, migration, cardiovascular development, neuronal migration, platelet morphology. Sources: UniProt P21333; Stossel et al., Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 2001
oncogenic_notes: Ambiguous DUAL role. Cytoplasmic FLNA promotes metastasis via VEGF, ERK, AKT. Nuclear 90 kDa fragment suppresses invasion via BRCA1. Flna KO reduces K-RAS-induced lung adenocarcinoma. Low FLNA also correlates with breast cancer progression. Targeting could paradoxically promote invasion. Sources: Savoy & Ghosh, PMC4376317; Bedolla et al., Clin Cancer Res 2009
isoforms_notes: Two main transcript variants. Calpain-cleavage products (190+90 kDa) are biologically significant. Soluble circulating form in patient plasma. No tumor-specific splice variants. Sources: UniProt P21333; Bu et al. 2012
toolbox_notes: Multiple intracellular-detection antibodies (MAB1678, MAB1680). Only 2-3 antibodies from Bachmann 2006 bind surface FLNA (unvalidated for ADC). M2 melanoma (FLNA-deficient), A7 (reconstituted). Flna conditional KO mice exist. No ADC benchmarks. Sources: Bachmann et al. 2006
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- no validated surface epitope for antibody binding.
key_concerns: Intracellular cytoskeletal protein; no validated TM domain; surface claim unvalidated; soluble FLNA decoy in plasma; platelet/immune sink; essential gene; dual oncogene/TSG role
recommendation: Absolutely excluded. Cytoskeletal protein without validated transmembrane domain.

surface_notes: ABSOLUTE DISQUALIFICATION. Peripheral membrane protein on INTRACELLULAR face of plasma membrane (palmitoylated on cytoplasmic side). Zero extracellular domain. Antibody cannot access this target on intact cells. Sources: UniProt P63092; Molecular Cancer 2025
internalization_notes: Not applicable. No extracellular domain = no antibody binding = no internalization possible. Sources: N/A
therapeutic_window_notes: Not applicable for ADC. Ubiquitously expressed core G-protein. GNAS activating mutations (R201H/C, Q227L) found in IPMN (40-75%), PMP (90%), pituitary adenomas (28%), cholangiocarcinoma (5-12%). Neoantigens suitable for vaccine, not ADC. Sources: HPA; Molecular Cancer 2025
pk_notes: Not applicable. Copy number on external surface = zero. Sources: UniProt P63092
safety_notes: Homozygous KO: embryonic lethal (E10.5). LOF causes pseudohypoparathyroidism type Ia, progressive osseous heteroplasia, McCune-Albright syndrome. Essential for hormonal signaling in all endocrine tissues. Complex imprinting. Sources: MGI Gnas; MedlinePlus GNAS; PMC4417430
competition_notes: No ADC programs exist or can exist. Therapeutic approaches: peptide vaccine (Pseudovax Phase I in PMP), cyclic peptide inhibitors (GN13, GD20), downstream inhibitors (trametinib), CRISPR/ASOs. All non-antibody modalities. Sources: PMC8557294; AACR 2024 CT079; Molecular Cancer 2025
physiology_notes: Stimulatory G-protein alpha subunit coupling activated GPCRs to adenylyl cyclase -> cAMP -> PKA. Regulates hormonal responses (PTH, TSH, ACTH, gonadotropins), beta-adrenergic signaling, metabolism, bone development. GNAS locus is imprinted (Gsalpha, XLalphas, NESP55, A/B). Sources: MedlinePlus GNAS; GeneCards
oncogenic_notes: Validated oncogene (gsp oncogene). Activating mutations at R201/Q227 cause constitutive activation -> elevated cAMP -> PKA -> proliferative signaling. Found in IPMN, PMP, pituitary adenomas, cholangiocarcinoma (5-12%), CRC (4-5%). Strong oncogene but entirely intracellular. Sources: Molecular Cancer 2025; JCO 2024; Nature Genetics 2012
isoforms_notes: 77 Ensembl transcripts. Products: Gsalpha long/short, XLalphas (paternal), NESP55 (maternal, secreted), A/B transcript. None create extracellular antibody-accessible epitopes. Sources: GeneCards; UniProt P63092
toolbox_notes: Multiple intracellular-detection antibodies. No antibodies targeting extracellular domain (none exists). Cell lines with GNAS mutations available. Conditional KO mice exist. Pseudovax peptides developed. No ADC benchmarks possible. Sources: VectorBuilder; PMC8557294
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- zero extracellular domain; biophysically impossible to target with antibodies.
key_concerns: Zero extracellular domain (biophysical impossibility); intracellular face only; ubiquitous; essential gene; embryonic lethal KO
recommendation: Absolute non-negotiable exclusion for antibody-based modalities. Correct modalities: neoantigen vaccines, small molecule inhibitors, gene therapy.

surface_notes: Type I TM with large ECD (~550 aa, 5 cadherin repeats). Validated surface protein. However, primarily sequestered within desmosomal junctions, limiting antibody accessibility. Pathogenic pemphigus antibodies bind non-junctional Dsg1 at EC1-EC2 domains. Sources: UniProt Q02413; GeneCards; HPA
internalization_notes: No direct ADC internalization data. Anti-Dsg3 antibodies trigger internalization in keratinocytes (pemphigus studies). Desmosomal cadherins undergo constitutive endocytic recycling. Internalized material does NOT colocalize with lysosomal markers (LAMP-1 negative) -- non-lysosomal trafficking is a critical ADC disqualifier. Sources: Amagai et al.; PubMed 18505410
therapeutic_window_notes: INVERSE OF ADC REQUIREMENT. DSG1 restricted to squamous epithelia and LOST/DOWNREGULATED in tumors: HNSCC (all SCC cell lines lost DSG1), lung SCC, ESCC (FC=-1.89). Not expressed in non-squamous cancers (CCA, mesothelioma). Loss = poor prognosis in HNSCC. Sources: MCR 2019; DSG1 in HNSCC (ScienceDirect); PubMed 38073377
pk_notes: Significant shedding: ECD cleaved by staphylococcal exfoliative toxins, SpeB protease, metalloproteinases. Shed ectodomains act as soluble decoys in MMP-rich TME. No blood cell expression. Copy number on accessible tumor surfaces likely very low. Sources: PubMed 14630910; Frontiers 2018
safety_notes: Heterozygous LOF: striate palmoplantar keratoderma. Homozygous LOF: SAM syndrome (severe dermatitis, allergies, metabolic wasting -- life-threatening). Anti-DSG1 autoantibodies cause pemphigus foliaceus (skin blistering). ADC would mimic pemphigus. DSG1 is a tumor suppressor (suppresses EGFR/Erk via Erbin). Sources: OMIM; PMC3613937
competition_notes: No ADC programs targeting DSG1. Anti-DSG3 with ADCC explored for lung SCC (PMC6267343). Absence reflects fundamental unsuitability. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: Desmosomal cadherin in stratified squamous epithelia. Beyond adhesion: suppresses EGFR/Erk/MAPK signaling via Erbin, controls keratinocyte differentiation, modulates paracrine signaling to melanocytes for UV-protective tanning, regulates cytokine production. Sources: Harmon et al. (JCI); Hammers & Stanley, PMC3613937
oncogenic_notes: TUMOR SUPPRESSOR. Suppresses EGFR/Erk signaling; restoring DSG1 in HNSCC cells suppresses invadopodia and invasion. Loss = poor prognosis in HNSCC. Melanoma cells actively repress Dsg1 in surrounding keratinocytes via CXCL1/CXCR2. Not amplified or overexpressed in any priority tumor. Sources: MCR 2019; JCB 2023
isoforms_notes: 2 Ensembl transcripts. Soluble truncated ectodomain fragments (~45, ~80 kDa) from proteolytic cleavage. Propeptide cleaved by furin during maturation. No tumor-specific isoforms. Sources: PubMed 12948916
toolbox_notes: Excellent antibody toolbox (pemphigus research): validated mAbs (27B2, 18D4, 32-2B, DSG1/1733, EPR20382). Commercial ECD ELISAs and recombinant proteins. However, most SCC cell lines have LOST DSG1. HaCaT keratinocytes express DSG1. DSG1 KO mice and pemphigus passive transfer models available. Sources: Abcam ab12077; MBL ELISA
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- target absent from tumors; antibody binding would cause pemphigus-like skin toxicity.
key_concerns: Tumor suppressor lost in priority tumors; non-lysosomal trafficking (LAMP-1 negative); pemphigus-like blistering toxicity; desmosomal sequestration; ectodomain shedding; SAM syndrome from LOF
recommendation: Unsuitable: inverse of ADC requirement (present on normal tissue, absent from tumors). Pemphigus precedent proves anti-DSG1 antibodies cause severe skin blistering.

surface_notes: Multi-pass (4 TM, claudin superfamily). Two small ECLs: ECL1 ~50 aa and ECL2 ~25 aa. Anti-CLDND1 antibody recognizing ECL1 generated (Matsuoka 2017). Unlike CLDN18.2/CLDN6, lacks tumor-restricted expression. Sources: OMIM 619677; Matsuoka et al., J Biochem 2017
internalization_notes: No CLDND1-specific internalization data. Claudin internalization generally slower than conventional ADC targets due to tight junction sequestration. Anti-CLDN18.2 (zolbetuximab) undergoes internalization. No ADC PoC. Sources: General claudin ADC literature
therapeutic_window_notes: Predominantly brain-expressed with no tumor selectivity. High in: corpus callosum, caudate, cortex, medulla, spinal cord (myelinated structures, oligodendrocytes). Component of BBB tight junctions. Low tissue specificity overall. Possible survival factor in breast cancer. No systematic analysis in priority cancers. Sources: Fayein et al. 2002; PubMed 30734065
pk_notes: No direct shedding evidence. Serum CLDND1-derived peptide antibodies elevated in cerebral infarction patients (BBB breakdown). BBB endothelial expression = antigen sink + BBB disruption risk. Small ECLs further limit accessible antigen density. Sources: Matsuoka et al. 2018
safety_notes: Brain expression: abundant in myelinated structures and BBB tight junctions. De novo CLDND1 A249P mutation causes Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like leukodystrophy (nystagmus, truncal hypotonia, seizures). CLDND1 downregulation increases vascular permeability and stroke risk. Sources: OMIM 619677; Hashimoto et al. 2024; Shima et al. 2021
competition_notes: No ADC or therapeutic programs. CLDN18.2 (zolbetuximab approved, multiple ADCs) and CLDN6 (BioNTech CAR-T/ADCs) have tumor-restricted patterns that CLDND1 lacks. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
physiology_notes: Tight junction protein contributing to paracellular barrier function. Component of BBB. Expressed in oligodendrocytes (CNS myelinating cells). Classified as regulatory (not barrier/channel-forming) claudin. Critical for vascular integrity. Sources: Matsuoka et al. 2017; Shima et al. 2021; Hashimoto et al. 2024
oncogenic_notes: Neither clear oncogene nor tumor suppressor. Knockdown induces apoptosis in basal-like breast cancer (possible survival factor). Z38/CLDND1 overexpressed in breast cancer promoting proliferation. No published evidence in any priority cancer type. Sources: Achari et al., PLOS One 2015; J Cancer 2016
isoforms_notes: 3 protein-coding isoforms: a (253 aa, canonical), b (278 aa), c (158 aa). No dominant soluble isoform. No tumor-specific isoforms characterized. Short isoform c might have altered topology but uncharacterized. Sources: OMIM 619677; NCBI Gene 56650
toolbox_notes: Multiple polyclonal antibodies (ThermoFisher PA5-91879). Anti-ECL1 research antibody (Matsuoka et al.). No therapeutic-grade anti-ECL mAbs. Cell lines: MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, BT-549, MCF-7. Mouse Cldnd1 KO strains available (18 in IMSR). No ADC benchmarks. Sources: ThermoFisher; Matsuoka et al.; JAX MGI
bispecific_rationale: Not applicable -- brain/BBB expression creates unacceptable safety risk regardless of gating strategy. Unlike CLDN18.2/CLDN6, lacks tumor-restricted expression.
key_concerns: 4-TM with small ECLs; brain/BBB dominant expression; no tumor selectivity; LOF leukodystrophy; BBB disruption risk; eclipsed by CLDN18.2/CLDN6
recommendation: Excluded. Lacks the tumor-restricted expression that made CLDN18.2/CLDN6 successful claudin targets. Brain/BBB localization creates both safety liability and antigen sink.

protein_name: Scavenger Receptor Class B Type I (SR-BI)
surface_notes: Type III TM (2 TM domains) with large ~400 aa extracellular loop -- excellent epitope space. Localizes to plasma membrane caveolae. Heavy N-glycosylation (9 sites). HPA confirms membranous staining in adrenal cortex, hepatocytes, Leydig cells. Sources: UniProt Q8WTV0; OMIM 601040; HPA
internalization_notes: Documented endocytosis via clathrin and caveolae pathways. HCV entry receptor validates internalization. HDL particles processed in endocytic pathway. No ADC-specific internalization studies. Sources: Reactome R-HSA-2512800; Cell Commun Signal 2023
therapeutic_window_notes: Overexpressed in prostate cancer (persists in metastases), breast cancer, NPC (75%), CRC. High normal tissue expression in adrenal gland (very high), liver (sinusoids), placenta. Sources: Cancer Research 2019; HPA; Frontiers Pharmacol
pk_notes: Alternative splice variant SR-BII exists. Present on monocytes but not highly on RBCs/platelets. High liver sinusoidal expression may cause hepatic clearance. Copy number unknown. Sources: J Lipid Research
safety_notes: FAVORABLE: No severe LOF phenotypes. P297S variant causes elevated HDL-C without severe outcomes. Mouse KO viable (abnormal HDL, female infertility, not lethal). Not essential. NOT a tumor suppressor -- promotes tumor growth via cholesterol delivery. Low heart/brain expression. Sources: OMIM 601040; Am J Hum Genet
competition_notes: WHITE SPACE: No SCARB1-targeted ADCs. Small molecule inhibitors (BLT-1) research-only. HDL-mimetic nanoparticles explored for drug delivery. First-in-class opportunity. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
bispecific_rationale: Liver and adrenal expression create meaningful sink; AND-gate with tumor-restricted target would improve therapeutic window.
key_concerns: Adrenal gland expression (very high) -- steroid deficiency risk; liver sinusoidal expression -- hepatic sink; no ADC-specific internalization studies
recommendation: Most promising candidate in R8. Appropriate topology, documented endocytosis, tumor overexpression (prostate, CRC), no severe safety signals, competitive white space. Needs: copy number quantification, antibody internalization validation, in vivo tolerability.

surface_notes: Type I TM with exceptionally large ECD (515 kDa alpha-chain, 4 ligand-binding clusters, 31 complement-type repeats). Precursor cleaved by furin into alpha+beta chains (non-covalently associated). Excellent topology. Sources: UniProt Q07954; HPA
internalization_notes: Best-in-class: t1/2 ~0.5 min via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. NPxY and YxxL motifs drive rapid constitutive internalization. Lysosomal trafficking for cargo degradation + efficient receptor recycling. Clinical validation via Angiopep-2/ANG1005 (Phase II brain metastases). Sources: PMC2744109; ANG1005 clinical trials
therapeutic_window_notes: Overexpressed in GBM, ccRCC (poor prognosis), gastric, HCC, pancreatic. However, ubiquitously expressed: highest in hepatocytes, vascular smooth muscle, neurons. Brain and liver expression particularly high. Sources: HPA; TCGA; PubMed 30033103
pk_notes: Significant ectodomain shedding by ADAM10/12/17 and MT1-MMP. Soluble LRP1 circulates in plasma = decoy receptor. High macrophage expression affects biodistribution. Hepatic sink. Sources: Sheddase literature; plasma proteomics
safety_notes: Mouse KO embryonic lethal -- essential developmental function. No direct human LOF genetic disease (likely embryonic lethal). Critical roles in brain (amyloid-beta clearance), liver, vasculature (SMC function). Complex cancer biology: both promoting and suppressive. LRP1B is a validated tumor suppressor. Sources: OMIM; mouse KO studies
competition_notes: No direct ADC programs targeting LRP1 as cytotoxic antigen. Angiopep-2 conjugates (ANG1005) use LRP1 for brain delivery. Multiple nanoparticle programs exploit LRP1 for CNS penetration. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov
bispecific_rationale: Ubiquitous normal expression requires AND-gate. Low-affinity anti-LRP1 arm + high-affinity tumor-specific anchor (Mesothelin, TROP2). Best suited for GBM where BBB crossing and tumor expression align.
key_concerns: Ubiquitous expression (liver + brain = dual toxicity risk); ectodomain shedding creates soluble decoy; essential developmental gene; complex cancer biology
recommendation: Exceptional internalization (best-in-class) but substantial therapeutic window challenges. Consider only for GBM where BBB crossing and tumor targeting align. High-risk/high-reward profile.

surface_notes: 7-TM adhesion GPCR with autoproteolytic cleavage into extracellular NTF (3-5 EGF-like repeats + GAIN domain) and membrane-spanning CTF. Despite 7-TM, large NTF provides substantial extracellular epitope space. HPA confirms plasma membrane localization. Sources: UniProt P48960; HPA
internalization_notes: Published ADC PoC (2025): Anti-CD97 antibody (A8) targeting GAIN domain demonstrates efficient internalization and beta-arrestin recruitment. Site-specific PBD-dimer ADC killed AML and GBM cell lines and patient-derived GBM stem cells with validated lysosomal trafficking. Sources: PubMed 2025 (PMID 41026810); bioRxiv 2023
therapeutic_window_notes: Upregulated in GBM, AML, thyroid, CRC, gastric, pancreatic cancers. However, constitutively expressed on granulocytes, monocytes, activated lymphocytes, neutrophils. Bone marrow/whole blood 18x enrichment. Unfavorable prognostic marker in liver/lung SCC. Sources: HPA; TCGA
pk_notes: Strong expression on circulating immune cells (granulocytes, monocytes, neutrophils) = significant target sink diverting ADC from solid tumors. NTF (alpha subunit) shed in inflammatory conditions = soluble decoy. Multiple splice isoforms. Sources: HPA; PMC literature
safety_notes: No major LOF genetic diseases (OMIM). Not essential in DepMap. Low brain and heart expression are favorable. However, role in leukocyte migration/activation means depletion could cause immunosuppression. Sources: OMIM; DepMap; GeneCards
competition_notes: Academic ADC PoC for AML/GBM published 2025. No registered clinical trials for CD97 ADC. Research-stage novel target. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; PubMed 2025
bispecific_rationale: Immune cell sink requires AND-gate with solid tumor-restricted target for solid tumor indications. May be better as OR-gate partner for hematologic indications where immune cell expression IS the target.
key_concerns: Broad immune cell expression = major antigen sink; NTF shedding creates soluble decoy; diverts drug from solid tumors to hematopoietic compartment
recommendation: Validated ADC PoC with favorable internalization, but broad immune cell expression unsuitable for solid tumor priority indications. May be viable for AML/GBM. Better as Driver arm in bispecific format.

surface_notes: Type I TM with 2 extracellular Ig domains (IgV + IgC) and intracellular B30.2/SPRY domain. Large ECD (~224 aa) suitable for antibody targeting. However, ESCC IHC shows 'mainly located in cytoplasm and only few distributed on cell surface.' Sources: UniProt O00481; HPA; ESCC IHC studies
internalization_notes: No direct ADC internalization studies. Anti-CD277 antibodies (20.1, 103.2) functional in immune studies but internalization not characterized. B7 family generally shows moderate internalization. Critical data gap. Sources: Limited data
therapeutic_window_notes: Overexpressed in CCA, HNSCC, RCC, liver, stomach, gliomas, ovarian (HGSOCs), breast, cervical cancers. However, ubiquitously expressed including HIGH in heart, pancreas, lung. Strong expression on T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, macrophages. Whole blood 5.8x enrichment. Sources: HPA; TCGA
pk_notes: Strong immune cell expression (T cells, NK, DCs, macrophages) and high bone marrow expression = significant target sink. Shedding data unavailable. Copy number unknown. Sources: HPA
safety_notes: No LOF genetic diseases (OMIM). Not essential in DepMap. However, HIGH cardiac expression = cardiac toxicity concern. Tumor suppressor signal: BTN3A1 downregulated in 70.8% NSCLCs and 81.6% breast cancers. Functions as immune checkpoint with immunomodulatory effects. Sources: OMIM 613593; DepMap; cancer expression studies
competition_notes: No BTN3A1 ADC clinical trials. Active research on anti-CD277 agonist antibodies for immunotherapy (gamma-delta T cell activation). Target pursued for immunotherapy, not ADC. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; ImmunoOncology pipeline
bispecific_rationale: Cardiac expression and immune cell sink cannot be adequately addressed even with AND-gate bispecific.
key_concerns: High cardiac expression = cardiac toxicity risk; ubiquitous expression + immune cell sink; no internalization data; possible tumor suppressor (downregulated in NSCLC/breast)
recommendation: Excluded despite favorable Type I TM topology. High cardiac expression is a safety red flag. Immune cell sink would limit tumor delivery. Tumor suppressor signal concerning. Consider for gamma-delta T cell immunotherapy instead.

surface_notes: SECRETED CYTOKINE, not a cell surface receptor. Exists as membrane-bound precursor proteolytically cleaved and released as soluble disulfide-linked homodimer. The appropriate surface target is CSF1R (receptor), not CSF1 itself. Sources: UniProt P09603; GeneCards; HPA
internalization_notes: CSF1R (receptor) undergoes robust clathrin-mediated internalization with lysosomal trafficking, but this applies to the receptor, not the ligand. CSF1 cleared from circulation via receptor-mediated uptake. Not viable for ADC. Sources: Nature 2020; J Cell Sci; Blood 2012
therapeutic_window_notes: Ubiquitously expressed as cytokine, low tissue specificity. Highest RNA in ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma. CSF1/CSF1R overexpression in breast, ovarian, prostate, endometrial. As soluble factor, no tumor cell surface expression to target. Sources: HPA; TCGA
pk_notes: CRITICAL: Exists primarily as soluble/secreted form competing for antibody binding. Circulating CSF1 levels increase massively upon CSF1R blockade. Expression on monocytes/macrophages throughout body. Sources: Blood (ASH); Nature
safety_notes: CSF1 mutations in rodents cause severe osteopetrosis. CSF1R mutations cause Hereditary Diffuse Leukoencephalopathy with Spheroids. Loss of CSF1/CSF1R causes macrophage and osteoclast deficiency. CSF1R essential for microglia survival. Sources: OMIM 120420; OMIM 164770
competition_notes: Clinical programs target CSF1R (receptor), not CSF1: Pexidartinib (FDA-approved for TGCT), LY3022855, RG7155. No CSF1-targeted ADCs exist because targeting secreted cytokine is not viable. Sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; FDA approvals
bispecific_rationale: Secreted protein fundamentally unsuitable for any antibody-based targeting approach.
key_concerns: Secreted cytokine -- not a cell surface target; soluble form = massive decoy; cannot deliver payload to tumor cells; correct target is CSF1R (receptor)
recommendation: Fundamentally disqualified. Secreted cytokine, not a cell surface receptor. The appropriate target in this pathway is CSF1R.
